items.title: Josh Hart To Play Through Finger Injury Rather Than Undergo Career-Ending Surgery
items.summary: New York Knicks wing Josh Hart has abandoned plans for surgery on his right ring finger and will play through the pain for the rest of his career. Hart said Thursday the injury now requires a full joint replacement, which would end his NBA career. Hart explained why the procedure is not an option. "You can't have the banging, repetitive (motion)," said Hart. "Grabbing a rebound, palming it, shooting, catching the ball, doing all that: You can't do that. So, if I did a joint replacement, then I wouldn't be able to play." The 31-year-old will keep protecting the finger with a splint or wrap whenever he plays. Hart wore a splint throughout the 2025-26 season. Hart first hurt the finger during the 2025 Eastern Conference finals against the Indiana Pacers. Hart had surgery that offseason but aggravated it while guarding Mikal Bridges in a team scrimmage. He had planned to undergo a second operation after last season. Doctors told him this summer that a joint replacement was needed instead. Hart said he will likely have the procedure after he retires. The injury, which also affected a nerve, causes ongoing discomfort. "Some days, it'll be good. Some days it'll hurt to catch the ball," said Hart. "It varies. I wish I could tell you when I wake up, what's gonna be good, what's gonna be bad. Some days it's good, like a regular functioning finger; and other days, it hurts to just close my hand, to make a fist." Hart still produced the most efficient shooting season of his career in 2025-26, making a career-best 41% of his 3-point attempts and posted a career-high effective field-goal percentage. Hart is eligible for an extension but said at media day he did not expect one to get done. Hart is owed $43.3 million over the next two seasons, including a $22.4 million team option for 2027-28.

items.title: Mavericks Fully Guarantee 26-27 Contract For Moussa Cisse
items.summary: The Dallas Mavericks have fully guaranteed Moussa Cisse's contract for the 2026-27 season. Cisse will now make $2.2 million for this season. The deadline for Dallas to waive Cisse at a cost of $1.1 million was October 1. Cisse played well on a two-way contract with the Mavs last season. The 6-foot-11 big man averaged 4.5 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 13.9 minutes per game in 38 NBA appearances. The New York Knicks signed Cisse to an offer sheet this offseason. The Mavericks quickly matched that offer sheet to keep Cisse in Dallas. The Mavericks now have 15 players on the roster with fully guaranteed contracts. Dallas also recently re-signed veteran center Dwight Powell to a partially guaranteed deal. The Mavs reportedly intend to keep Powell on the regular season roster, which will necessitate another move to free up a roster spot.

items.title: Knicks, Rangers To Split Into Separate Publicly Traded Companies
items.summary: Investors will soon be able to buy stock in the New York Knicks and New York Rangers separately. MSG Sports announced Wednesday that its board approved dividing the NBA and NHL franchises into two publicly traded companies, with the transaction expected to close Oct. 26. The Knicks will belong to MSG Knickerbockers Corp., which will also own the G League's Westchester Knicks. MSG Rangers Corp. will hold the Rangers, the AHL's Hartford Wolf Pack and the MSG training facility. Trading begins on October 27th. The Knicks company will use the ticker "MSGK," while the Rangers company will trade as "MSGR." James Dolan will serve as executive chairman and CEO of both. Dolan outlined the reasoning in a statement. "With our board's approval we are now one step closer to our goal of separating our Knicks and Rangers businesses into two distinct public companies," said Dolan. "Both teams have storied histories and large and passionate fan bases, and we believe each company will be well-positioned to generate long-term value for shareholders." The split follows contrasting stretches for the two clubs. The Knicks captured the NBA championship in June. The Rangers are rebuilding after missing the playoffs in each of the past two seasons. MSG Sports reported $1.153 billion in revenue and $59 million in profit for the fiscal year that ended June 30. The Knicks' title run boosted the bottom line. The franchise generated $66.9 million more in playoff revenue than the prior year, despite playing nine games at Madison Square Garden in both postseasons. The company began exploring the separation earlier this year. Dolan previously moved the teams away from Madison Square Garden in a 2020 spin-off that placed the arena and franchises in different public companies. The Knicks signed a 35-year lease at the venue in 2021. The Knicks and Rangers remain among the few professional sports franchises owned by a publicly traded company.

items.title: Knicks Hoping For Karl-Anthony Towns Extension Closer To $200M Over Four Years
items.summary: The New York Knicks are navigating a challenging contract extension discussion with Karl-Anthony Towns and are significantly apart on a new number. The Knicks are "far more interested" in signing Towns to a contract closer to a four-year, $200 million deal compared to the four-year, $276 million extension he is eligible to sign, reports Jake Fischer at Bleacher Report . Towns is prepared to sign for less than his max, but the two sides are significantly apart on value. Towns can become a free agent during the 2027 offseason if they are unable to agree to terms on an extension. The Knicks are facing ongoing second apron issues and hope to bring down his 2027-28 player option worth $61 million. Towns is set to come off his four-year, $220 million supermax extension signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2022. Towns was an All-NBA player in his first season with the Knicks and was critical in their 2026 championship.
